messages.author: bfc2eb6b71169017
messages.subject: simple boxplot with no y
parts:
Dear list,

is it possible to circumvent the need to supply the y argument for ggplot? I would like to make a simple boxplot showing circumference of studied trees and the following line returns an error (as expected):

> boxy <- ggplot(obs_b)
Error: ggplot2 doesn't know how to deal with data of class numeric

What I am trying to achieve can be siply done by base boxplot(obs_b).


Cheers,
Roman

messages.author: cd9baedf48d871eb
messages.subject: Re: simple boxplot with no y
parts:
Actually, it's the x argument that you would like not to supply, if I
understand correctly what you want (i.e showing the distribution of
values in obs_b)

Furthermore, ggplot() takes as argument a dataframe (I suppose obs_b
is a numeric vector?), and layers must be added.
The quickest way to do what you want is, as its name suggests, qplot
().
So try:
qplot(x=factor(1), y=obs_b, geom="boxplot")
